description.full: La Tunda is one of the most feared supernatural entities in the folklore of Colombia's Pacific coast, particularly among Afro-Colombian communities in the departments of Chocó, Valle del Cauca, Cauca, and Nariño. She is a malevolent female shapeshifter who preys primarily on children, though adults are not immune to her deceptions. Her name comes from \"tundir\" (to beat or thrash), reflecting either her violent nature or the punishment children receive for wandering into her domain. The entity's most distinctive physical characteristic is her wooden leg—specifically, one foot takes the form of a molinillo, a traditional wooden kitchen utensil used to froth hot chocolate. This peculiar detail connects her to domestic spaces while simultaneously marking her as fundamentally inhuman. La Tunda represents a perfect synthesis of Afro-Colombian and Indigenous cultural elements, embodying ancestral fears about the dangers of the rainforest and serving as a powerful cautionary tale about obedience and safety.
